maintainer_comments.author: KellerJordan
maintainer_comments.body: Personally I would consider all of the changes described here to be 100% legitimate. Both @ClassicLarry and I have the power to accept new records— for me to accept I’d need to first reproduce this result myself, & I haven’t had time to do so yet.

maintainer_comments.author: ClassicLarry
maintainer_comments.body: I haven't gone through all the specifics yet, but at a high level I agree it looks great. Hoping to find a block of time soon to look at more closely and refactor the code into something easier to follow, now that we are jumping to 5k+ lines. I'd be curious to understand where the intuition came from on Sampled-softmax training loss and Embeddings, hashed n-gram table. And if any of the results are a joint effort across Social Physics Lab or Autoresearch harness on Codex (in the past groups have set records then after the fact revealed a larger initiative behind it, which is totally fine too). In any case, very impressive!

maintainer_comments.author: ClassicLarry
maintainer_comments.body: I am going to pass on this PR for now. With only 0.28s gain for a new optimizer, higher loss (requires more than 10 runs to hit p value <0.01), and based on an older branch that would need to be revalidated. The PR drops 6 steps to get the speedup, and its not super clear to me I can't get a similar-ish speedup from dropping 6 steps on the baseline and taking a slightly higher loss. Will come back and revisit at a future time once the open PRs are merged to see if there's a cleaner integration point with bigger wins.

maintainer_comments.author: ClassicLarry
maintainer_comments.body: This is a pretty creative idea. But I am not seeing an improvement when I run this on the current main. Getting 200ms slower and slightly higher less, at equal step count.

maintainer_comments.author: ClassicLarry
maintainer_comments.body: The most recently merged in PR changed the shape of the matrices for Q and K (mentioning in case this impacts this PR). I will look at this one in more detail later, looks like some neat stuff.

maintainer_comments.author: ClassicLarry

maintainer_comments.author: ClassicLarry
maintainer_comments.body: This direction looks promising to me, but might require Nsight Profiler deep dive to fully understand when these streams are getting scheduled. My concern is that if the hardware is deciding when to prioritize this cpu-to-gpu data transfer stream, it might block the main GPU stream in hard to detect ways. Im not sure on the best way to interleave this with the forward and backwards pass, but ideally we can do it in a way that executes consistently across different GPU providers.
